description.value: A remote wilderness campground in Vancouver Island's unprotected Central Walbran Valley, tucked amid ancient old-growth forest on Pacheedaht Nation territory; volunteer-maintained with outhouses, trails, and a visitor centre since 2012, but no cell service and rough forest-service road access.

raw_osm.description: A rustic campsite established by the Friends of Carmanah Walbran.
raw_osm.name: Central Walbran Valley

enrichment_extras.reasoning: OSM tags confirm a free campsite (fee=no) with toilets (toilets=yes) and no reservations required (reservation=no), operated by Friends of Carmanah Walbran. The website corroborates this directly: 'The Central Walbran has extensive trails, camp sites, outhouses and a visitor centre maintained by the Friends of Carmanah Walbran since 2012.' The website's active 2026 event planning at this location confirms the site is open and operational. No phone or physical address is available in either OSM or the website.
concerns: No physical address or phone number available in OSM or on the website.
Access is via remote logging roads; not practically reachable by road or light touring cyclists.
The website is the operator organization's site (Friends of Carmanah Walbran), not a dedicated campsite listing; no site-specific contact details are present.
Cougar sightings reported near Walbran bridge (late 2022 per trail info page) — safety context worth noting for visitors.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The campsite is genuine, free, actively maintained, and clearly operational, but access is via remote logging roads on Vancouver Island — a human reviewer should confirm whether the WWC directory scope includes bikepacking/gravel destinations of this remoteness.
enrichment_extras.notes: OSM confirms no fee (fee=no) and toilets present (toilets=yes); website confirms outhouses and a visitor centre on site. Driving instructions page exists on the website (/visit-the-central-walbran-driving-instructions/) but full content was not in the fetched pages.

wow_evidence: ancient old-growth forest on Pacheedaht Nation territory; volunteer-maintained with outhouses, trails, and a visitor centre since 2012
